f3_program: collection("facebook.employees", "employee", "facebook", source("Facebook employs 3300 employees"))
collection("facebook.employees.women.mothers", "employee", "facebook", source("all its female employees who are mothers"))
observe(at("facebook.employees.count", "current"), 3300, "count", source("Facebook employs 3300 employees"))
fraction_of(at("facebook.employees.men.count", "current"), at("facebook.employees.count", "current"), 1, 3, source("one-third are men"))

difference_relation(at("facebook.employees.women.count", "current"), at("facebook.employees.count", "current"), at("facebook.employees.men.count", "current"), source("one-third are men, and of the women"))
observe(at("facebook.employees.women.not_mothers.count", "current"), 1200, "count", source("of the women, 1200 are not mothers"))

difference_relation(at("facebook.employees.women.mothers.count", "current"), at("facebook.employees.women.count", "current"), at("facebook.employees.women.not_mothers.count", "current"), source("of the women, 1200 are not mothers"))
observe(at("facebook.annual_earnings", "2020"), 5000000, "currency", source("Facebook's annual earnings, which was $5,000,000 for the year 2020"))
percent_of("facebook.productivity_bonus.total", at("facebook.annual_earnings", "2020"), 25, source("This productivity bonus will total 25% of Facebook's annual earnings"))

quotient_relation("facebook.productivity_bonus.per_female_mother", "facebook.productivity_bonus.total", at("facebook.employees.women.mothers.count", "current"), source("assuming each one received an equal amount"))
query("value", "facebook.productivity_bonus.per_female_mother")
assumptions: The wording implies that employees are partitioned into men and women, and women into mothers and non-mothers.

f3_program: collection("john.purchased_puzzles", "puzzle", "john", source("John buys 3 puzzles"))
add("buy_puzzles", "john", at("john.purchased_puzzles.count", "current"), 3, source("John buys 3 puzzles"))

collection("john.purchased_puzzles.piece_counts", "piece_count", "john.purchased_puzzles", source("The first puzzle has 1000 pieces.  The second and third puzzles have the same number of pieces and each has 50% more pieces"))
member("john.purchased_puzzles.piece_counts", "john.purchased_puzzles.first.pieces.count", source("The first puzzle has 1000 pieces"))
member("john.purchased_puzzles.piece_counts", "john.purchased_puzzles.second.pieces.count", source("The second and third puzzles have the same number of pieces"))
member("john.purchased_puzzles.piece_counts", "john.purchased_puzzles.third.pieces.count", source("The second and third puzzles have the same number of pieces"))
observe(at("john.purchased_puzzles.first.pieces.count", "current"), 1000, "count", source("The first puzzle has 1000 pieces"))
same(at("john.purchased_puzzles.second.pieces.count", "current"), at("john.purchased_puzzles.third.pieces.count", "current"), source("The second and third puzzles have the same number of pieces"))
percent_more(at("john.purchased_puzzles.second.pieces.count", "current"), at("john.purchased_puzzles.first.pieces.count", "current"), 50, source("each has 50% more pieces"))
percent_more(at("john.purchased_puzzles.third.pieces.count", "current"), at("john.purchased_puzzles.first.pieces.count", "current"), 50, source("each has 50% more pieces"))
query("sum", "john.purchased_puzzles.piece_counts", "current")
assumptions: The elliptical comparison "50% more pieces" uses the first puzzle as its reference.

f3_program: collection("mitchell.book.pages_read_components", "page_count", "mitchell.book", source("the total number of pages that Mitchell had read altogether"))
observe(at("mitchell.book.full_chapters_read.count", "before_4_oclock"), 10, "count", source("Mitchell had read ten chapters of a book before 4 o'clock"))
observe(at("mitchell.book.chapter_11.pages_read.count", "4_oclock"), 20, "count", source("Mitchell had read 20 pages of the 11th chapter"))

same(at("mitchell.book.chapter_11.pages_read.count", "current"), at("mitchell.book.chapter_11.pages_read.count", "4_oclock"), source("After 4 o'clock, she didn't read the remaining pages of chapter eleven"))
add("read_two_more_chapters", "mitchell", at("mitchell.book.full_chapters_read.count", "current"), 2, source("read 2 more chapters of the book"))
observe(at("mitchell.book.pages_per_chapter", "current"), 40, "page_per_chapter", source("each chapter in the book had 40 pages"))

rate_relation(at("mitchell.book.full_chapters_read.pages.count", "current"), at("mitchell.book.pages_per_chapter", "current"), at("mitchell.book.full_chapters_read.count", "current"), source("each chapter in the book had 40 pages"))
member("mitchell.book.pages_read_components", "mitchell.book.full_chapters_read.pages.count", source("Mitchell had read ten chapters of a book before 4 o'clock"))
member("mitchell.book.pages_read_components", "mitchell.book.chapter_11.pages_read.count", source("Mitchell had read 20 pages of the 11th chapter"))
query("sum", "mitchell.book.pages_read_components", "current")
assumptions: The two chapters read after 4 o'clock are complete chapters distinct from chapter eleven.
